"'''Happy'''" is a song written, produced, and performed by American musician [[Pharrell Williams]], released as the only single from the [[Despicable Me 2 (soundtrack)|soundtrack album]] for the film ''[[Despicable Me 2]]'' (2013).{{Efn|The song "[[Just a Cloud Away]]", also from the soundtrack, was released as a single on March 24, 2022, after a resurgence in popularity due to [[TikTok]].}} The song was first released on July 2, 2013 with the soundtrack, and it was released as a single on November 21, 2013, alongside a 24-hour-long [[music video]]. The song was reissued on December 16, 2013, by [[Back Lot Music]] under exclusive license to [[Columbia Records]], a division of [[Sony Music Entertainment|Sony Music]].<ref name="USrelease"/> The song also served as the lead single from Williams's second studio album, ''[[Girl (Pharrell Williams album)|Girl]]'' (2014). An official remix features American rapper [[Sky Blu (rapper)|Sky Blu]] of [[LMFAO]].

"Happy" is an uptempo [[Soul music|soul]] and [[neo soul]] song on which Williams's [[falsetto]] voice has been compared to [[Curtis Mayfield]]'s by critics. The song has been highly successful, peaking at No. 1 in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, [[Ireland]], New Zealand, and 19 other countries. It was the best-selling song of 2014 in the United States with 6.45 million copies sold for the year,<ref name="US Sales">{{cite web|first= Paul |last= Grein |title= It's Official: Pharrell Has 2014's Best-Selling Song |publisher= [[Yahoo! Music]] |date= December 31, 2014 |access-date= April 22, 2015 |url= https://www.yahoo.com/music/its-official-pharrell-has-2014s-best-selling-106748836876.html}}</ref> as well as in the United Kingdom with 1.5 million copies sold for the year.<ref name="Top 40">{{cite web|first= Rob |last= Copsey |title= The Official Top 40 Biggest Selling Singles of 2014 |publisher= [[Official Charts Company]] |date= January 1, 2015 |access-date= January 1, 2015 |url= http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/the-official-top-40-biggest-selling-singles-of-2014-3389/}}</ref> It reached No. 1 in the UK on a record-setting three occasions and became the most downloaded song of all time in the UK in September 2014;<ref>{{cite web|first= Rob |last= Copsey |title= Pharrell's Happy now the UK's most downloaded track of all time |publisher= Official Charts Company |date= September 9, 2014 |access-date= April 22, 2015 |url= http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/pharrells-happy-now-the-uks-most-downloaded-track-of-all-time-3108/}}</ref> it is the [[List of best-selling singles in the United Kingdom|ninth-highest-selling single of all time in the country]].<ref name="uk sales"/> It was nominated for an [[Academy Award for Best Original Song]]. A live rendition of the song won the [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance]] at the [[57th Annual Grammy Awards]].

The music video for "Happy" was nominated for [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Male Video|Best Male Video]] and [[MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year|Video of the Year]] at the [[2014 MTV Video Music Awards]]. It also won the [[Grammy Award for Best Music Video]] at the 57th Annual Grammy Awards.<ref name="MTV2"/><ref name="MTV"/> The song was ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''{{'}}s number-one single for 2014. "Happy" was the most successful song of 2014, with 13.9 million units (sales plus equivalent streams) worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|title= IFPI publishes Digital Music Report 2015 |publisher= [[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry]] |date= 14 April 2015 |page= 12 |access-date= 15 April 2015 |url= http://www.ifpi.org/news/Global-digital-music-revenues-match-physical-format-sales-for-first-time |archive-date= 14 April 2015 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150414194629/http://www.ifpi.org/news/Global-digital-music-revenues-match-physical-format-sales-for-first-time |url-status= dead}}</ref> In 2024, the song appeared on the [[Piece by Piece (soundtrack)|soundtrack]] to the LEGO animated biography of Williams' life, ''[[Piece by Piece (2024 film)|Piece by Piece]]''.

"Happy" is a song written, produced, and performed by American musician Pharrell Williams, released as the only single from the soundtrack album for the film Despicable Me 2 (2013).{{Efn|The song "Just a Cloud Away", also from the soundtrack, was released as a single on March 24, 2022, after a resurgence in popularity due to TikTok.}} The song was first released on July 2, 2013 with the soundtrack, and it was released as a single on November 21, 2013, alongside a 24-hour-long music video. The song was reissued on December 16, 2013, by Back Lot Music under exclusive license to Columbia Records, a division of Sony Music. The song also served as the lead single from Williams's second studio album, Girl (2014). An official remix features American rapper Sky Blu of LMFAO.

"Happy" is an uptempo soul and neo soul song on which Williams's falsetto voice has been compared to Curtis Mayfield's by critics. The song has been highly successful, peaking at No. 1 in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, and 19 other countries. It was the best-selling song of 2014 in the United States with 6.45 million copies sold for the year, as well as in the United Kingdom with 1.5 million copies sold for the year. It reached No. 1 in the UK on a record-setting three occasions and became the most downloaded song of all time in the UK in September 2014; it is the ninth-highest-selling single of all time in the country. It was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Original Song. A live rendition of the song won the Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance at the 57th Annual Grammy Awards.

The music video for "Happy" was nominated for Best Male Video and Video of the Year at the 2014 MTV Video Music Awards. It also won the Grammy Award for Best Music Video at the 57th Annual Grammy Awards. The song was Billboard{{'}}s number-one single for 2014. "Happy" was the most successful song of 2014, with 13.9 million units (sales plus equivalent streams) worldwide. In 2024, the song appeared on the soundtrack to the LEGO animated biography of Williams' life, Piece by Piece.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
Williams provided vocals for French duo [[Daft Punk]]'s 2013 album ''[[Random Access Memories]]'' on the songs "[[Lose Yourself to Dance]]" and "[[Get Lucky (Daft Punk song)|Get Lucky]]". After returning from the recording sessions in [[Paris]], he attended a meeting with record label managers who said that the results were "spectacular" and that "Get Lucky" would be Daft Punk's next single. They also made Williams an offer to record his own album, to which he agreed quickly, "overwhelmed that someone wanted to know what's in my heart".<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Angus |last= Batey |title= We Heard Pharrell's New Album & This Is What It Sounds Like |magazine= [[NME]] |date= February 21, 2014 |access-date= March 20, 2014 |url= https://www.nme.com/blogs/nme-blogs/we-heard-pharrells-new-album-this-is-what-it-sounds-like}}</ref>

On December 17, 2013, it was announced that Williams had signed to [[Columbia Records]] and would release his second studio album in 2014.<ref name="Vibe">{{cite magazine|title= Pharrell Williams Signs to Columbia Records |magazine= [[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]] |date= December 17, 2013 |access-date= March 20, 2014 |url= http://www.vibe.com/article/pharrell-williams-signs-columbia-records}}</ref> Williams originally wrote the song for [[CeeLo Green]] and felt Green's recording of the song was better, but [[Elektra Records]], Green's record label, decided against it since he was on the verge of releasing his Christmas album, ''[[Cee Lo's Magic Moment]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first= Bang |last= Showbiz |title= Pharrell Williams – Pharrell Williams: Happy was for Cee Lo Green |publisher= [[Contactmusic.com]] |date= May 1, 2014 |access-date= May 1, 2014 |url= http://www.contactmusic.com/story/pharrell-williams-happy-was-for-cee-lo-green_4175044}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first= Ryan |last= Reed |title= Pharrell Says 'Happy' Originally Recorded by Cee Lo Green |magazine= [[Rolling Stone]] |date= April 30, 2014 |access-date= March 23, 2019 |url= https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/pharrell-says-happy-originally-recorded-by-cee-lo-green-247481/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first= Sean |last= Michaels |title= Pharrell Williams' Happy was originally recorded by Cee Lo Green |newspaper= [[The Guardian]] |date= April 30, 2014 |access-date= March 23, 2019 |url= https://www.theguardian.com/music/2014/apr/30/pharrell-williams-happy-was-originally-recorded-by-cee-lo-green}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first= Jimmy |last= Blake |title= Pharrell's Happy originally recorded by Cee Lo Green |work= [[Newsbeat]] |date= May 1, 2014 |access-date= March 23, 2019 |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/newsbeat-27234842}}</ref>

"Happy" is an up-tempo [[Soul music|soul]] and [[neo soul]] song.<ref name="Tingen">{{cite magazine|first= Paul |last= Tingen |author-link= Paul Tingen |title= Inside Track: Happy |magazine= [[Sound on Sound]] |location= Cambridge |date= May 2014 |access-date= October 23, 2014 |url= http://www.soundonsound.com/sos/may14/articles/inside-track-0514.htm}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first= Ali |last= Ryland |title= Wireless Festival 2014: From OutKast to Pharrell, the top ten acts to watch |newspaper= [[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]] |date= July 1, 2014 |access-date= May 25, 2015 |url= http://metro.co.uk/2014/07/01/wireless-festival-2014-from-outkast-to-pharrell-the-top-ten-acts-to-watch-4766164/}}</ref> According to music journalist [[Paul Tingen]], "Happy" is "a mid-tempo ... song in a faux-[[Motown]] style, with an arrangement that is, by modern standards, very sparse: programmed drums, one bass and one keyboard part, and handclaps both programmed and played, all topped off by Williams's lead vocals and a whole posse of backing vocals".<ref name="Tingen"/> [[Jody Rosen]] viewed the song as a "standout" with a "sprightly [[neo soul|neosoul]] [[funk]] [[Groove (music)|groove]]".<ref name="RS">{{cite magazine|first= Jody |last= Rosen |title= Pharrell – Happy |magazine= [[Rolling Stone]] |date= June 7, 2013 |access-date= November 23, 2013 |url= https://www.rollingstone.com/music/songreviews/happy-20130607 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130613052247/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/songreviews/happy-20130607 |url-status= dead |archive-date= June 13, 2013}}</ref>

"Happy" was met with very positive reviews. Jody Rosen of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' gave it 3.5 stars and deemed it "an instant contender for 2013's Song of the Summer".<ref name="RS"/> In a 4/5 review, ''[[Renowned for Sound]]''{{'}}s Huw Woodward said, "Happy is a rather... well... happy affair with a cheerful beat and exuberant vocal that would indicate that the former [[N.E.R.D.]] singer is finding a lot of lighthearted fun to be had in both music and life. 'Because I'm happy, clap along if you feel like happiness is the truth' sings Williams as the jaunty rhythm gets your head nodding."<ref name="RfS">{{cite web|first= Huw |last= Woodward |title= Single review: Pharrell Williams – 'Happy' |date= January 16, 2014 |work= Renowned for Sound |access-date= February 16, 2014 |url= http://renownedforsound.com/index.php/single-review-pharrell-williams-happy/}}</ref> Holly Williams of ''[[Contactmusic.com]]'' gave it four stars, praising it for being "unbelievably catchy" and "the kind of song that makes you want to dance and sing along".<ref name="CM">{{cite web|first= Holly |last= Williams |title= Pharrell Williams – Happy Single Review |date= 6 January 2014 |publisher= [[Contactmusic.com]] |access-date= March 3, 2014 |url= http://www.contactmusic.com/single-review/pharrell-williams-happy}}</ref> Reggie Ugwu of ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' called the song "Contagiously peppy and brilliantly simple".<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Reggie |last= Ugwu |title=Pharrell, 'G I R L': Track-By-Track Review |date= 25 February 2014 |magazine= [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date= May 1, 2023 |url= https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/pharrell-g-i-r-l-track-by-track-review-5915748/}}</ref> "Happy" was nominated for [[Academy Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]] at the [[86th Academy Awards]] on March 2, 2014, but lost to "[[Let It Go (Disney song)|Let It Go]]" from ''[[Frozen (soundtrack)|Frozen]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title= 2013 Nominations |publisher= [[International Press Academy]] |access-date= August 19, 2015 |url= http://www.pressacademy.com/award_cat/current-nominees/ |archive-date= April 19, 2014 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140419014132/http://www.pressacademy.com/award_cat/current-nominees/}}</ref> In January 2015, "Happy" was ranked at No. 13 on ''[[The Village Voice]]''{{'}}s annual year-end [[Pazz & Jop]] critics' poll.<ref>{{cite news|title= Singles: All Votes |newspaper= [[The Village Voice]] |date= January 2014 |access-date= 31 October 2018 |url= http://www.villagevoice.com/pazznjop/singles/ |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150120001020/http://www.villagevoice.com/pazznjop/singles/ |archive-date= 20 January 2015 |url-status= dead}}</ref>

Retrospective reviews have been more critical. In 2022, ''Far Out'' placed "Happy" on its "The 10 worst songs to have spent 10 weeks at Number 1 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]" list: "Featuring nonsensical lyrics such as 'clap along if you feel like a room without a roof,' it's a fine enough song for a children's film. However, there was no need for such a repetitive song to receive so much general radio play."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://faroutmagazine.co.uk/the-10-worst-10-weeks-at-number-one/|title=The 10 worst songs to have spent 10 or more weeks at number one|date=18 October 2022 |publisher=Far Out|access-date=April 30, 2023|author-first1=Aimee|author-last1=Ferrier}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Stereogum]]'' in his ''The Number Ones'' column, Tom Breihan gave the song a 3/10, calling it "a repetitive song, one that keeps running its chorus back and doesn't have a proper bridge."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Breihan |first1=Tom |title=The Number Ones: Pharrell's 'Happy' |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2262796/the-number-ones-pharrells-happy/columns/the-number-ones/ |date=13 May 2024 |website=[[Stereogum]] |access-date=14 May 2024}}</ref>

sections.text: In October 2013, a month prior to its single release, "Happy" catapulted to No. 1 on the Dutch Top 40 chart in the Netherlands, partially as a result of radio station 3FM airplay and subsequent online downloads, as well as featuring in a Transavia commercial. It went on to finish number five on the year-end Single Top 40 list, giving Williams three songs in the top five, along with "Blurred Lines" and "Get Lucky", both of which feature him.

sections.heading: United Kingdom
sections.wikitext:
In the United Kingdom, "Happy" debuted at No. 71 on the [[UK Singles Chart]] on December 1, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title= Official Singles Chart Top 100: 01 December 2013 – 07 December 2013 |publisher= Official Charts Company |date= December 7, 2013 |access-date= April 10, 2015 |url= http://www.officialcharts.com/charts/singles-chart/20131201/7501}}</ref> It then spent four weeks climbing before finally reaching No. 1 on December 29, becoming the final UK number one single of 2013.<ref name="UKC"/> It became Williams' third No. 1 song in Britain, counting "Get Lucky" and "Blurred Lines", where he appeared as a featured artist.<ref>{{cite news|first= Amy |last= Duncan |title= X Factor winner Sam Bailey's reign lasts just one week as she is knocked off No.1 spot by Pharrell |date= December 29, 2013 |newspaper= [[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]] |access-date= March 3, 2014 |url= https://metro.co.uk/2013/12/29/x-factor-winner-sam-baileys-reign-lasts-just-one-week-as-she-is-knocked-off-no-1-spot-by-pharrell-4244740/}}</ref> It has since spent four non-consecutive weeks at No. 1, reaching the peak on three separate occasions. In doing so, Williams became only the third artist ever to achieve this, and the first since [[Guy Mitchell]] in 1957 with "[[Singing the Blues]]".<ref name="UK"/> Following the single's third week at No. 1, it spent five weeks in the top three before returning to the summit, boosted by his performance at the [[2014 Brit Awards]].<ref name="UK"/> In the same week that "Happy" returned to No. 1 for the third time, it sold its millionth copy in the UK, Williams' third in under a year, having previously done so with Daft Punk's "Get Lucky" in June 2013, and Thicke's "Blurred Lines" in July 2013. This made Williams only the second artist in UK chart history (the first being [[the Beatles]]) to have three singles sell 1 million copies in under a year,<ref name="UK"/> as well as only the third artist ever to have three million-sellers, along with the Beatles (who have six) and [[Rihanna]] (who has four).<ref name="UK">{{cite web|first= Justin |last= Myers |title= Unstoppable Pharrell scores chart record hat-trick as Happy smashes a million |publisher= Official Charts Company |date= March 2, 2014 |access-date= March 3, 2014 |url= http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/unstoppable-pharrell-scores-chart-record-hat-trick-as-happy-smashes-a-million-2790/}}</ref>

In the United Kingdom, "Happy" debuted at No. 71 on the UK Singles Chart on December 1, 2013. It then spent four weeks climbing before finally reaching No. 1 on December 29, becoming the final UK number one single of 2013. It became Williams' third No. 1 song in Britain, counting "Get Lucky" and "Blurred Lines", where he appeared as a featured artist. It has since spent four non-consecutive weeks at No. 1, reaching the peak on three separate occasions. In doing so, Williams became only the third artist ever to achieve this, and the first since Guy Mitchell in 1957 with "Singing the Blues". Following the single's third week at No. 1, it spent five weeks in the top three before returning to the summit, boosted by his performance at the 2014 Brit Awards. In the same week that "Happy" returned to No. 1 for the third time, it sold its millionth copy in the UK, Williams' third in under a year, having previously done so with Daft Punk's "Get Lucky" in June 2013, and Thicke's "Blurred Lines" in July 2013. This made Williams only the second artist in UK chart history (the first being the Beatles) to have three singles sell 1 million copies in under a year, as well as only the third artist ever to have three million-sellers, along with the Beatles (who have six) and Rihanna (who has four).

"Happy" was the best-selling single of UK in 2014, with 1.5 million copies sold for the year, and became the most downloaded song of all time in the UK by September 2014, with over 1.62 million sold. It had also been streamed over 25 million times and was the first song released in the 2010s to go 3× Platinum. With the inclusion of streaming, "Happy" has achieved combined sales of over 2 million. Additionally, "Happy" and Idina Menzel's "Let It Go" became the first singles ever to spend an entire calendar year on the official UK top 75 chart. On June 12, it was announced that "Happy" had overtaken "Evergreen" by Will Young as the UK's best-selling single of the 21st century, with sales of 1.81 million. "Happy" spent 92 weeks in the UK top 100. {{as of|2020|February}}, the song has sold 1,950,000 copies.

sections.text: In May 2014, a group of Iranian fans who created a tribute to "Happy" were arrested. According to a police chief, the song represented vulgarity and also hurt public chastity. Williams responded to the arrest in a tweet stating "It's beyond sad these kids were arrested for trying to spread happiness." Soon after Iran's President Hassan Rouhani criticized the arrest when he tweeted "#Happiness is our people's right. We shouldn't be too hard on behaviours caused by joy." The dancers, along with the director, were later released. It was reported on September 19, 2014, that seven of the individuals in the Iranian video had been handed sentences, suspended for three years, of 91 lashes each along with jail by Iranian courts.

{{main|Tacky (song)}}
In 2014, American musician [["Weird Al" Yankovic]] parodied "Happy" as "[[Tacky (song)|Tacky]]" on his fourteenth studio album ''[[Mandatory Fun]]''. The song mocks questionable style in fashion as well as activities considered gauche. Yankovic recorded the song as one of the last on ''Mandatory Fun'', and received Williams' approval directly, through email. He remarked he was "honored" to have his work spoofed by Yankovic.<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Gary |last= Graff |title= 'Weird Al' Yankovic on Getting Pharrell's Permission: 'He Could Not Have Been Nicer' |magazine= Billboard |date= July 15, 2014 |access-date= June 4, 2021 |url= http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6157636/weird-al-yankovic-interview-pharrell-mandatory-fun}}</ref> The song's one-shot music video parodies "Happy", and was the first in a series of eight videos released over eight days in promotion of ''Mandatory Fun''. {{main|Tacky (song)}}
In 2014, American musician "Weird Al" Yankovic parodied "Happy" as "Tacky" on his fourteenth studio album Mandatory Fun. The song mocks questionable style in fashion as well as activities considered gauche. Yankovic recorded the song as one of the last on Mandatory Fun, and received Williams' approval directly, through email. He remarked he was "honored" to have his work spoofed by Yankovic. The song's one-shot music video parodies "Happy", and was the first in a series of eight videos released over eight days in promotion of Mandatory Fun. It features cameo appearances by Aisha Tyler, Margaret Cho, Eric Stonestreet, Kristen Schaal, and Jack Black, and was produced by Nerdist Industries.
